payload.title: Deactivate ad units from the console
payload.problem_statement: The ad units list shows each unit's status, but an operator has no way to deactivate one. The backend's PATCH /api/inventoryunit/status endpoint sets status to ACTIVE only, and the console never calls it, so taking a unit out of service means going outside this tool.
goals: Let the status-update endpoint set an ad unit to INACTIVE as well as ACTIVE.
Give the ad units list an action that deactivates the selected units.

user_stories.need: deactivate ad units I select in the console
user_stories.benefit: I can take a unit out of service without leaving the admin tool
acceptance_criteria: Selecting ad units and choosing deactivate sends those ad unit ids to the status endpoint with an INACTIVE target status.
The list reflects the new status after the request succeeds.

requirements.description: Extend the existing PATCH /api/inventoryunit/status endpoint to accept an explicit target status of ACTIVE or INACTIVE and apply it to the supplied ad unit ids. When the field is omitted the endpoint must keep its current behaviour of activating.
acceptance_criteria: The request validation accepts an optional status field whose value is ACTIVE or INACTIVE and rejects any other value.
A request with status INACTIVE sets those ad units to the INACTIVE status value already defined in the repository's status constants.
A request with no status field still activates, so existing callers are unaffected.
The change is covered by tests in the repository's existing backend test suite.

requirements.description: Add a deactivate action to the console's ad units list that sends the selected ad unit ids to the status endpoint with the INACTIVE target status and refreshes the list.
acceptance_criteria: The ad units API client module gains a request function that targets the status endpoint with a PATCH method and carries the selected ad unit ids and the INACTIVE status.
The ad units list renders a deactivate action that is disabled when no ad unit is selected.
The list data is refetched after a successful deactivate response.
The change is covered by a test in the console repository using its existing React testing setup.

constraints: Follow each repository's existing code style, lint rules, and test framework.
Do not add a database migration or change the ad unit schema; the status field already exists.
Do not change existing endpoint paths or the response shapes of existing endpoints.
Do not introduce a new status value; use the status vocabulary the repository already defines.
out_of_scope: Archiving ad units or any Google Ad Manager synchronisation.
Bulk deactivation through the existing Python archive script.

payload.title: Deactivate ad units from the console
payload.solution_summary: Extend the existing PATCH /api/inventoryunit/status endpoint so callers can explicitly set supplied ad unit IDs to the repository-defined ACTIVE or INACTIVE status while preserving the current ACTIVE default when status is omitted. Add a deactivation action to the console ad units list that submits selected IDs with status INACTIVE and refreshes list data after a successful response. No schema, endpoint-path, existing-response-shape, permission, archive-script, or Google Ad Manager synchronization changes are included.

functional_requirements.description: Extend PATCH /api/inventoryunit/status request handling to accept an optional status field, apply the requested repository-defined ACTIVE or INACTIVE status to the supplied ad unit IDs, and preserve existing activation behavior when status is omitted.
acceptance_criteria: The endpoint request validation accepts an omitted status field and accepts status values ACTIVE and INACTIVE using the repository's existing status vocabulary or constants.
The endpoint rejects a request containing a status value other than ACTIVE or INACTIVE according to the repository's existing validation and error-handling conventions.
A valid request containing status INACTIVE updates the supplied ad unit IDs to the repository-defined INACTIVE status constant.
A valid request with no status field continues to update the supplied ad unit IDs to the repository-defined ACTIVE status constant.
The existing endpoint path and response shape are unchanged.
Backend tests in the repository's existing test suite cover explicit INACTIVE behavior, omitted-status ACTIVE compatibility, and invalid-status rejection.

functional_requirements.description: Add a deactivate action to the console ad units list that deactivates selected ad units through the existing status endpoint and refreshes list data after a successful request.
acceptance_criteria: The console ad units API client exposes a function that sends a PATCH request to /api/inventoryunit/status with the selected ad unit IDs and status INACTIVE.
The ad units list renders a deactivate action following existing console UI conventions.
The deactivate action is disabled when no ad unit is selected.
Invoking the enabled deactivate action sends the currently selected ad unit IDs with status INACTIVE.
After a successful deactivate response, the list's existing data-fetch or refresh mechanism is invoked so the displayed statuses are refreshed.
Console tests using the repository's existing React testing setup cover disabled-without-selection behavior, the INACTIVE status request, and refresh after a successful response.

non_functional_requirements.description: Implement the backend and console changes using each repository's established code style, lint rules, request abstractions, UI patterns, and test framework.
acceptance_criteria: Changed source files follow the conventions evident in adjacent endpoint, API-client, and ad-units-list code.
The repositories' applicable existing lint, type-check, build, and test commands complete successfully for the changed code.
The implementation reuses existing status constants or vocabulary rather than defining a new status value.

non_functional_requirements.description: Keep the status-update operation limited to validation and the existing status update path; the console request must not block the interface beyond its existing asynchronous request lifecycle.
acceptance_criteria: The backend implementation performs no archive workflow, Google Ad Manager synchronization, schema migration, or unrelated external side effect as part of processing the status update.
The console uses the repository's existing asynchronous API request pattern and refreshes only after a successful response.
The code change does not add polling, retries, or new background processing for deactivation.

data_requirements: Use the existing ad unit status field; do not add a database migration or change the ad unit schema.
The status request field is optional for backward compatibility.
When provided, status is limited to the repository-defined ACTIVE and INACTIVE values.
The status endpoint continues to receive the existing supplied ad unit ID collection format; no request or response shape changes are introduced.
The console sends the currently selected ad unit IDs and the literal or repository-defined INACTIVE status value through the existing status endpoint contract.
integration_requirements: Use the existing PATCH /api/inventoryunit/status endpoint; do not add or change endpoint paths.
The console API client must issue a PATCH request compatible with the endpoint's existing request payload format, augmented only by the optional status field.
The console must use its existing ad units list data-fetch or refetch mechanism after a successful status update.
No Google Ad Manager synchronization, archive-script integration, or new external service integration is part of this work.
security_requirements: Do not change roles, permissions, authentication, or authorization behavior; the existing endpoint access controls remain in effect.
Preserve existing backend request validation and error-handling conventions for invalid status input.
Do not expose new sensitive data or alter existing endpoint response shapes.
assumptions: ACTIVE and INACTIVE are existing valid status values represented by repository-defined constants or an equivalent established vocabulary.
PATCH /api/inventoryunit/status already accepts the selected ad unit IDs in a format the console can send without changing the endpoint contract beyond the optional status field.
The backend and console may reside in separate repositories, each with its own established test and build commands.
The existing console list has a selection mechanism and an established data-refetch mechanism that can be reused.
Existing authorization permits the same users who can access the current status endpoint and ad units list to perform this action; no permission changes are requested.
No confirmation dialog, optimistic update behavior, error-message behavior, or post-action selection-clearing behavior is specified; existing console conventions should be retained.

unresolved_questions.question: What is the exact existing request payload key and ID collection shape used by PATCH /api/inventoryunit/status?
unresolved_questions.rationale: The PRD identifies the endpoint and supplied ad unit IDs but does not specify the precise payload contract; implementation must preserve it while adding the optional status field.

unresolved_questions.question: Should the deactivate action be available for all selected ad units, including units already marked INACTIVE, or should it be conditionally disabled or filtered based on status?
unresolved_questions.rationale: The PRD requires disabling only when no unit is selected and does not define behavior for mixed or already-inactive selections.

unresolved_questions.question: What existing console convention should govern user-visible failure handling, confirmation, and selected-row state after a deactivation request?
unresolved_questions.rationale: Success refresh behavior is defined, but error feedback, confirmation requirements, and whether selection is retained are not specified and may affect the UI implementation.

payload.system_overview: The feature extends the existing authenticated inventory-unit status endpoint in Ad Manager Server to accept an optional target status while retaining ACTIVE as the omitted-status default. AB Console Admin consumes that unchanged endpoint through its existing ad-unit API utility and adds a per-row deactivate control to the AdUnits table. The action submits the row adUnitId as a one-element adUnitIds array with status INACTIVE, refreshes the existing list only after success, and reports failures through the established snackbar pattern.

technology_stack.backend: Node.js/Express, Joi validation, Mongoose-style AdunitModel access, Jest
technology_stack.frontend: JavaScript React/Next.js console, reusable table cell renderers, notistack, React Testing Library/Jest

components.responsibility: Receives validated status-update requests, delegates the supplied IDs and optional target status, and preserves the existing successful message response.

components.name: Inventory unit status service
components.responsibility: Updates existing ad-unit status values using ACTIVE when status is omitted and the requested validated ACTIVE or INACTIVE value when supplied.

components.name: Console ad-unit status API client
components.responsibility: Builds the authenticated PATCH request configuration for the existing inventory-unit status endpoint with a one-element ID array and INACTIVE status.

components.responsibility: Provides a per-row deactivation control, disables it for an already INACTIVE row, invokes the API client, refreshes data after success, and enqueues a failure snackbar.

components.responsibility: Registers the deactivate cell renderer with the existing table framework components and adds its column to the existing ad-unit column definitions.
components.technology: React page and table column utilities

api_contracts.summary: Sets the status of supplied inventory-unit IDs to ACTIVE or INACTIVE; omitted status remains backward-compatible and defaults to ACTIVE.

decisions.title: Extend the existing status endpoint
decisions.decision: Add optional status validation and status propagation to the existing PATCH /api/inventoryunit/status path rather than creating a deactivation endpoint.
decisions.rationale: The established endpoint already accepts adUnitIds, has existing authentication and response behavior, and the requested change is limited to selecting ACTIVE or INACTIVE.
consequences: Existing clients omitting status continue to activate ad units.
No endpoint path, response shape, schema migration, or new status vocabulary is introduced.

decisions.title: Use per-row deactivation rather than list selection
decisions.decision: Implement a deactivate control in each eligible ad-unit row and submit only that row ID as a one-element adUnitIds array.
decisions.rationale: Checkout reconnaissance establishes that the console has no row-selection state or table selection mechanism, while the backend contract already accepts an array.
consequences: No multi-select or checkbox infrastructure is added.
The control is disabled for rows already in INACTIVE status.
The PRD selection-oriented wording is fulfilled by the current row rather than unsupported bulk selection.

decisions.title: Refresh after confirmed success
decisions.decision: Invoke the existing AdUnits refetchData mechanism only after the deactivation request succeeds; report failure with enqueueSnackbar.
decisions.rationale: This follows the established console asynchronous request and list-refresh conventions and avoids optimistic state mutation.
consequences: Displayed statuses are reloaded from the existing list source after success.
No polling, retry, background processing, confirmation dialog, or selection-clearing behavior is added.

decisions.title: Use isolated unit tests
decisions.decision: Test backend service/controller behavior directly with model mocks and test the frontend cell renderer in isolation with the API utility mocked.
decisions.rationale: The server has no safe assembled-app HTTP test harness, and importing the broader console page/router path reaches a pre-existing ESM parsing defect.
consequences: No new HTTP integration harness or test configuration is introduced.
Tests cover request payloads, ACTIVE fallback, INACTIVE updates, invalid validation behavior, refresh, and error handling through isolated units.

risks.description: The repository has parallel legacy and nested ad-unit route/controller/service structures, so changing the wrong grouping would leave the live endpoint unchanged.
risks.mitigation: Change and test the nested server/routes/adunits, server/controllers/adunit, server/services/adunit, and server/validation modules identified for the /status route; preserve route registration.

risks.description: Console test imports that reach AdUnits routing or CreateBatch can fail because of a pre-existing nanoid ESM transform configuration defect.
risks.mitigation: Keep the new React test isolated to the table-cell component and mock the API utility; do not import AdUnits.js, routeUtils, Router, or CreateBatch.

risks.description: The PRD initially assumes selected-row support, but the checked-in console does not have selection infrastructure.
risks.mitigation: Use a per-row action with a one-element adUnitIds payload and do not introduce unrelated table-selection infrastructure.

payload.deployment_strategy: Deploy the backward-compatible backend change before the frontend. The endpoint remains compatible with existing activation callers because status is optional and defaults to ACTIVE; deploy the console after the backend is available, then roll back the console independently if needed.

payload.summary: Added the inventory-unit status PATCH API utility and an isolated deactivate action cell with disabled inactive-state handling, successful refresh behavior, failure notifications, and React tests for the row action.

findings.title: Optional status is not propagated through the status update path
findings.description: The only production change is the Joi schema in server/validation/adUnit.validation.js. No bounded source change exists in the nested status controller or service to pass a validated status to the update operation, apply explicit INACTIVE, or default an omitted status to ADUNIT_STATUS.ACTIVE. Consequently, the implemented updateInventoryUnitStatus contract behavior is not evidenced and may remain hard-coded to the prior activation behavior.
findings.recommendation: Update the existing nested inventory-unit status controller and service so the controller forwards the optional validated status and the service uses status ?? ADUNIT_STATUS.ACTIVE in its updateMany $set operation. Preserve the existing PATCH route, authorization middleware, and {message} success response.
findings.evidence: workspace_change_evidence contains only server/validation/adUnit.validation.js and server/tests/adunitStatus.test.js; neither provides controller/service status propagation or update behavior.
findings.recommended_fix: Modify the identified nested status controller/service implementation and add the status argument to the existing service call, with ADUNIT_STATUS.ACTIVE as the omitted-status fallback in the service.

findings.title: Required direct controller and service status tests are absent
findings.description: server/tests/adunitStatus.test.js tests only the Joi schema. It does not mock AdunitModel to verify updateMany filters and explicit INACTIVE/omitted ACTIVE values, nor does it test controller success behavior with mocked request, response, and service dependencies.
findings.recommendation: Extend server/tests/adunitStatus.test.js, or add focused adjacent tests, with direct mocked service/model and controller tests. Verify explicit INACTIVE reaches updateMany, omitted status results in ACTIVE, supplied adUnitIds are used in the update filter, and the controller returns the existing message response shape.
findings.evidence: The test file imports only adUnitValidation and ADUNIT_STATUS and contains three Joi validation cases; it imports neither the status controller/service nor AdunitModel.
findings.recommended_fix: Add direct Jest tests using mocked AdunitModel access for service updateMany assertions and mocked req/res/service dependencies for controller success assertions, without importing the assembled Express application.

payload.architecture_assessment: The validation-layer addition is appropriately narrow and uses the established ADUNIT_STATUS vocabulary, but the endpoint behavior spans validation, controller, and service layers. The controller/service portion required to implement the approved status-update contract is absent from the bounded changed source.
payload.security_assessment: The schema whitelists status to the existing ACTIVE and INACTIVE constants, preserving invalid-input rejection for the newly accepted field. No changed source alters authentication, authorization, sensitive-data exposure, or response serialization; however, end-to-end application of only the validated value cannot be confirmed until propagation is implemented.
payload.test_coverage_assessment: Required commands passed: npm run lint, npm run test, and npm run build. The new Jest coverage directly verifies omitted, ACTIVE, INACTIVE, and invalid validation inputs, but it lacks the required direct service updateMany and controller success-response coverage for explicit INACTIVE and omitted-status ACTIVE behavior.

payload.summary: admanager-server is an Express-based server repository containing JavaScript controllers, routes, services, Mongoose-style models, middleware, validation modules, and Python Google Ad Manager utility scripts.
